title: Price Watch

examples.explanation: The waits are 2, 1, 2, 1, 1 and 0. Day 1's price 3 is first beaten on day 3 (price 4), day 3's price 4 is first beaten on day 5, and nothing beats day 6. They add up to 7.
The price never goes strictly higher, so every wait is 0.

hints: For each day, scanning forward until a higher price is O(n) per day. A strictly decreasing run of prices makes that O(n²) in total.
Scan left to right and keep the days that are still waiting for a higher price. What do their prices look like, read from the oldest to the newest?
The waiting days always have non-increasing prices, so a stack works: when today's price beats the top, the top's wait is decided. Every day is pushed once and popped at most once.
The total can reach about n²/2 ≈ 2 · 10¹⁰. Use a 64-bit integer.
